title: Bunk's Selmer trumpet, cornet and mouthpiece
summary: Blumberg and Russell discuss how Bunk handled the Selmer, tried Blumberg's King cornet and his mouthpiece.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Uh. Well, uh, to change the subject again, speaking of horns, I just happened to think about it, uh, did Bunk ever say and make any remarks about his Selmer trumpet, if he liked it, or?

I think he liked it. He certainly handled it as if he liked it, but, uh, he tried my cornet. I was playing a King cornet at the caravan one night, and, and, uh, he sounded kind of different on the thing. And, uh, we were all very interested, you know, to hear, uh, how he sounded on it. And, uh, he, he liked the horn. He, he, he said he thought it was a very fine horn. Maybe there was just nostalgia for, for playing a cornet. Maybe he just, uh, actually wanted to be playing a cornet the whole time.
I understood he always wanted the con cornet, actually, because we got him the Selmer thing at a bargain without knowing that it wasn't his favorite and all that, too.
Well, he sure got a nice sound out of that Selmer. Yeah. I mean, it, uh.
Did he use your mouthpiece when he played it? Yeah, I guess he did. He had to, I guess.
Well, it was, I, I imagine it was similar to, to the one that he was using. I was using pretty stupid.

He had an old French mouthpiece, a Cuesnone, I can't pronounce it, C-U-E-S-N-O-N. Oh, yeah. And, uh, had a new shank, an old cornet mouthpiece, and he had a new, uh, Rudy Muck put a new shank on it and replated it. Mm-hmm. So he couldn't tell what it was, but I think he always used that most of his late years. Mm-hmm. Did he ever give you any advice on mouthpieces? No. On mouthpieces?

No. No, he never did. I, I, uh, I thought the mouthpiece he had looked kind of standard, as I recall, the looks of it. I think so. It looked like about a, could have been a ten, ten and a half C Bach, uh, mouthpiece. Mm-hmm. From the looks of it.
It wasn't extra deep, but it certainly wasn't shallow, as I remember.
No, I don't think it was a cushion rim type thing.
No, not a big rim or anything, as I can remember. Dave Bell has that, I guess.
Oh, is that right? He still has the horn. I'm sure he'd never get rid of it.
